featured_reviews.name: rohan vaswani
featured_reviews.review_text:
My Experience with Piramal Group – Repeated Defaults on Written Commitments

I am sharing this purely as my personal experience and opinion, based on direct interactions with Piramal Group’s senior representatives.

I was given multiple explicit assurances, including a specific written commitment that a credit note would be issued by 8 February. That promise has now been missed, repeatedly, without explanation, ownership, or even basic communication—despite escalations to senior management.

When an organisation of this scale fails to honour simple, routine financial commitments after multiple follow-ups, it raises serious concerns about internal accountability, governance, and execution discipline. What is most worrying is not the delay itself, but the complete absence of transparency or ownership.

As a customer, this experience has significantly eroded my confidence. Repeated missed timelines and silence create the unfortunate perception that commitments are made casually and honoured selectively.

I would strongly advise prospective customers to document everything in writing, be cautious with assurances, and factor in delays—even when commitments are made at senior levels.

This review reflects my experience alone, but it has been deeply disappointing.

featured_reviews.name: Rajkunwar Pawar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointed with the After-Sales Experience

I would strongly advise against booking a property here. The after-sales service has been extremely poor, and the customer relationship management is frustrating to deal with. The CRM team seems to be trained only to follow up for payments and installations — any genuine customer concerns are consistently ignored.

We received an official invite claiming the amenities were completed and ready for viewing. We travelled from another city just for this, only to find that barely 10% of the amenities were ready — just two indoor rooms (Pilates & Cycling). This was highly misleading.

Despite making multiple visits — including two personal trips I made flying in from London — we have still not been shown the floor view of the completed building (South), even though that is a basic request. Our unit is in a different tower, but our only request was to see the floor view of a completed tower. Every time, we’ve been met with excuses like “we don’t have the keys” — even though possession hasn’t started yet.

The customer service is apathetic at best. Calls go unanswered, and emails regarding even simple customer requirements are ignored.

If this is the service before possession, it raises serious concerns about what can be expected after moving in.

featured_reviews.review_text:
DO NOT BOOK. Read this:
1. SRA: Humungous SRA kissing back of north and central towers. For upto 20 floors,  you'll litrally wake up next to SRA residents, if you are in units facing behind. This giant SRA is just the start. These guys have over 10 acres behind PM, which can lead to more SRAs in future.
2. Access road: 2 access roads. Babu Sakpal road is filthy beyond imagination. I gagged multiple times when I was surveying neighborhood. Never smelled anything so bad. This is also entry to SRA. Police petroling very frequent here. Other access is through Arthur road, 2 blocks from Arthur Rd. jail. So you can expect some disturbance on that.
3. Builder quotes: Please read each line on cost sheet very carefully. They've quoted different price everytime I visited. They'll push you for really unacceptable units in north tower. Review GST charges carefully. They know exactly where all they've messed up. So they'll only show higher floor in south tower to you.
4. Possible criminal activities in area: The SRA behind has 50+ units per floor and 40+ floors. These SRA units are already selling in black market. You can imagine what kind of people will buy these 400 sq. ft. units for a cr. Let me give you a hint, they're not going to be slum dweller. Still not clear? Read Saat rasta history.
Builder finish is good, but does not compensate for negatives. Worth waiting for OC so you can at least see what you're paying for in this strangely marketed/ located property. Mahalaxmi is good real estate micromarket, but avoid this property for sure.

featured_reviews.review_text: We are a apartment complex amidst the hustle bustle of Business District @LowerParel. We are here since 2006 July. featured_reviews.name: Brij Agarwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Living at Lodha Park feels like you’ve stepped out of South Mumbai once you enter — calm, green, and peaceful.

The 7-acre garden is a huge plus, and all amenities like pools, tennis, squash, and even a restaurant are well maintained and actually usable.

Great construction and planning — you can see the thought behind the project. Full credit to Lodha for having a Vision to create something like this back in 2012.

Overall, a complete lifestyle inside the complex — rare to find in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Hem Meisheri
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Lodha Park in Worli, and I must say, it is truly impressive. The ambiance of the place is nothing short of luxurious, with meticulous attention to detail in every aspect. The entire building exudes a sense of elegance and comfort, making it one of the finest residential options in the area.

The cleanliness of Lodha Park is outstanding. The staff is exceptionally good, always alert and conscious of their duties. They ensure that every corner of the property is spotless and well-maintained, adding to the overall appeal of the place.

One of the standout features of Lodha Park is its extensive range of amenities. There are 3 towers spread across 17 acres of land. The cricket ground, club house, and luxurious pools provide residents with plenty of options for recreation and relaxation. The high-speed lifts make accessing the 65 floors quick and convenient, reflecting the modernity and efficiency of the building. Parking is ample and well-organized, which is a big plus for residents with vehicles.

The greenery around Lodha Park is another highlight. The lush surroundings and scenic beauty create a serene and peaceful environment, which is quite rare in a bustling city like Mumbai. It’s a perfect place for families to enjoy nature while being in the heart of the city. The canteen is an added convenience, offering a variety of food options for residents.

Overall, Lodha Park stands out as one of the best places for a family to live. The combination of luxury, cleanliness, excellent staff, and top-notch amenities makes it a premier choice in Worli.

featured_reviews.name: Pragya Sethy (Prags)
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been staying here for the past five years. The society itself is good, and the neighbors are also friendly and cooperative. However, the major drawback is the surrounding area.
The entrance to the society passes through a slum, which creates several ongoing issues. There is no designated parking available for visitors, and the area often faces disturbances from the slum residents. At times, they block the road for their personal functions, causing inconvenience to residents.
Additionally, many of the slum households use their residential spaces for commercial purposes, operating shops on the ground floor. This leads to lorries and small trucks being parked along the road, making it extremely difficult for four-wheelers to pass through.
Another concern is that the road is often treated as private parking by them. If any visitors park near the society wall or even pass through, they sometimes create a nuisance or even damage vehicles, claiming ownership over the public road.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Amarnath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sethia Sea View, Goregaon West – Deteriorating Condition Over the Years

I’ve been visiting Sethia Sea View in Motilal Nagar 3, Goregaon West regularly because my sister-in-law stays here, and over the years, I’ve witnessed the building deteriorate significantly. 5 - 6 years back it used to look really good.

🚧 Building Condition:
The building, which once used to be well-maintained and classy, is now in very bad condition. The paint is peeling off, and the overall state of the building has deteriorated. Although there are ongoing efforts to repaint it, it’s been taking forever.

🚗 Access & Parking Issues:
The narrow lanes that lead up to the building, especially through the slums, create a lot of inconvenience. Parking is also a major issue, as there’s no parking space for visitors. It’s frustrating that such a large building doesn’t provide basic visitor parking, something that is essential for residents and their guests.

🔊 Noise Pollution:
Another major problem is the noise pollution. The mosque next door creates a lot of noise in the mornings, making the environment far from peaceful. Additionally, noisy bikers often zoom through the narrow lanes at night, disrupting the peace at late hours like 12 AM or 1 AM.

❌ Overall Experience:
While it was once a nice place to stay, Sethia Sea View is no longer in good shape. The deteriorating condition of the building, combined with accessibility issues and noise pollution, make it hard to recommend as a living space.
